label: Team Lead
description: Between an employee and a manager: leads the people who report to them (their direct reports, `my-reports`) on goals and 1:1s, and decides none of their requests. Everything an employee holds, plus setting, coaching and agreeing the direct reports' goals and running their check-ins. Leave, attendance, expenses, timesheets, reviews and rosters stay with the department manager and HR.
relies_on: The reporting line. `my-reports` is the people whose manager is the team lead (employees.manager), resolved per caller at decision time - so a lead reaches exactly the people assigned to them, and moving someone to another lead moves the access with them, with no rule to edit.

levels.why: Set and edit the direct reports' goals - the reason the role exists. A goal created for a report passes the owner-on-create gate because the lead writes `goals.<their code>`.
Run 1:1s with the direct reports: notes, action items, the next meeting. Owner-coded under the report, so only the lead's own reports' check-ins.
The goal blueprint catalogue, to set goals from it. Authoring the catalogue stays HR's.

allow.why: Agree a goal a report proposed. A proposal is sent to the report's direct manager (services/goals.ts proposeGoal), which is the lead - without this the goal-setting handshake would stall on someone told to act who cannot. Agreeing a goal is part of setting it, not a request decision.
Send a proposed goal back with the reason - the other half of agreeing it.
The on-track / at-risk call on a report's goal the lead set.
Coach on a report's goal; the thread under a goal is where that happens.
Overlapping goals across the reports, and what a report's goal should align to - decided against the lead's own goal scope.
A unit, start and target for a report's goal that has none, offered while agreeing it.
Stamp a blueprint onto the direct reports. The apply service checks write on `goals.<code>` for every person named, so a lead can only apply it to their own reports.

excluded.pattern: <requests>.my-reports.approve | reject (leave, attendance corrections, overtime, remote work, late/early, assets, timesheets, expenses)
excluded.why: A team lead decides no requests. They stay with the department manager (`my-dept`) and HR.
Not needed to set goals or run 1:1s, and leave carries medical reasons. An org whose leads plan rosters grants the read in Access Management.
Presence is read off leave and attendance, which a lead does not see; confirming probation is the manager's call.

The performance review - manager assessment, 360 nominations, evidence pack, record copy - is the department manager's. A lead's input reaches it through 1:1 notes and goal comments, and through 360 feedback when nominated.
Crediting a share of a goal scores in the contributor's review, so it is a statement about somebody's performance - the manager's call.
Running the team's boards is the manager's; a lead works the cards like any employee.
Rostering stays with the manager and HR.
